minutes.headline: Finance Committee heard the Budget Task Force's 20 recommendations and began planning the FY26 budget calendar; no budget votes.
minutes.summary: The Budget Task Force presented its 20 recommendations (investment policy, a targeted audit, the Community Preservation Act, solar, Brooks House, trash, Chapter 90, health insurance options, fees, snow removal consolidation, split tax rate). The chair outlined a backward-planned budget season calendar, and updates were given on the town manager search, capital planning, FY24 year-end and Chapter 70 minimum aid. The only votes were approving minutes and adjourning.

public_comment.topic: Suggested DLS free services for auditing, cautioned that consolidating accounts may remove check-and-balance redundancy after past fraudulent invoices, and urged study of a local income tax.

Commented that the task force work was good but may not answer whether the town has enough money for FY26; worried about health insurance projections, prioritization against the municipal building project, and Chapter 70 funding.
Update on the 211 communities minimum-aid Chapter 70 effort and Representative Scarsdale's work.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee heard the Budget Task Force present its 20 recommendations, from an investment policy and a targeted audit to a split tax rate.
Members agreed in discussion that the task force recommendations should be tracked with actions through to conclusion; no budget votes were taken.
The chair asked for four meetings after the public hearing, planned back from a 25-day warrant deadline before the May 2nd town meeting.
Members heard that Lunenburg receives the minimum per-pupil Chapter 70 increase while other communities receive larger percentage increases.
The chair will put the budget season schedule on the January 9th agenda and check the preliminary budget timing with the town manager.

why_it_matters: The task force list touches the tax bill and town services (trash and recycling costs, health insurance, snow removal, a split tax rate), but nothing was decided; each item is still a proposal that would need later votes.
Chapter 70 state aid is a large part of school funding and, as discussed, grows more slowly than expenses, so the FY26 budget gap depends on a figure the town does not set.
